text_blocks.snippet: Opsumit (macitentan) is an oral medication used to treat pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH). Like all prescription drugs, it can cause both common and serious side effects.
The most frequent side effects reported in clinical studies include:

list.snippet: Nasopharyngitis (common cold symptoms or stuffy/runny nose)
Bronchitis or upper respiratory tract infections
Anemia (low red blood cell count, usually occurring during the first weeks of treatment)
Urinary tract infections (UTIs) and influenza (flu-like symptoms)
Peripheral edema (swelling in the hands, lower legs, or feet)

Serious Birth Defects: Opsumit can cause severe harm or death to an unborn baby. It is strictly contraindicated during pregnancy, and females who can become pregnant must have a negative pregnancy test before starting treatment, take regular tests, and use reliable contraception.

Liver Damage (Hepatotoxicity): Opsumit can affect liver function. Doctors typically check liver enzymes before starting treatment and monitor them periodically. Seek medical help right away if you notice signs of liver problems, such as yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice), dark urine, severe right-sided upper stomach pain, nausea, vomiting, or unusual fatigue.

Fluid Retention: Excess fluid buildup or worsening swelling can happen, particularly during the first few weeks of therapy. Notify your doctor if you experience rapid weight gain or trouble breathing.
Decreased Sperm Counts: Opsumit may reduce sperm counts and impact male fertility.
